open: In the name of Allah. Assalamu alaikum, my dears. Come closer, tonight’s story is very beautiful.
s1a: Noah… Ilyas… Imagine: you are sharing a bar of chocolate. Each of you should get the same. But one of you secretly takes an extra piece. Is that fair?
s1c: Exactly. Get warm and cosy… Today I’ll tell you about the Prophet Shuaib, peace be upon him. Allah sent him to the people of Madyan.
s2a: The people of Madyan did not worship Allah alone. And they cheated with weight and measure: when they sold something, they gave people less than their due.
s2c: Not always, my dear. If a scale is secretly rigged, nobody notices. And they also sat on the roads threatening people, and keeping those who believed in Allah away from the way of Allah.
s3a: Shuaib was one of them. Allah says: “And to the people of Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said, ‘O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So fulfill the measure and weight and do not deprive people of their due and cause not corruption upon the earth after its reformation. That is better for you, if you should be believers.’” That means: give people their full due when you weigh.
s3b: Shuaib reminded them that they had been few and Allah had increased them. And he told them that he only wanted to set things right as much as he could, that his success was only through Allah, that he relied on Him and turned back to Him.
s3c: And did they listen to him?
s4a: No. They said to him: O Shuaib, does your prayer command you that we should leave what our fathers worship, or not do with our wealth what we please?
s4b: What? But what does prayer have to do with that?
s4c: A big connection, my dear! Allah says: “Recite, O Muhammad, what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows that which you do.” That means: prayer keeps us away from bad things, and Allah knows what we do, even in secret.
s5a: But the leaders of the town threatened Shuaib: either you come back to our religion, or we will drive you out of the town, you and those who believe with you! Shuaib answered that they rely on Allah, and he prayed: Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who decide.
s5c: Allah saved Shuaib and those who believed with him. As for the others, who did not want to listen, the punishment came to them as the Qur’an tells us: a violent shaking, a strong quake, and a mighty blast. And their homes became as if they had never lived in them.
s6a: Allah says: “And he turned away from them and said, ‘O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how could I grieve for a disbelieving people?’” That means: I will not be sad for a people who did not believe.
s6b: And what do we learn from this, Grandma?
s6c: We learn that honesty is very important! Allah says: “Woe to those who give less than due, who, when they take a measure from people, take in full. But if they give by measure or by weight to them, they cause loss.” That means: when they buy for themselves they take everything, but when they sell to people they give them less.
s6d: And our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by a pile of food. He put his hand into it, and his fingers felt wetness. He said: What is this, owner of the food? He said: The rain fell on it, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Why did you not put it on top of the food, so that people could see it? Whoever cheats is not from me.
s6e: So we have to show it even if something isn’t good?
s6f: Exactly, my clever dear. Being honest means: hiding nothing.
s7a: Oh… they’ve fallen asleep. My dears… always be honest. When you share, when you play, and when you swap things. Give others what is rightfully theirs. And remember: Allah sees everything, even what happens in secret.
s7b: And next time, I’ll tell you about Musa… and about a little baby in a little chest, floating on a big river. And you, watching us right now: if you liked the story, ask your parents to subscribe to our channel, so you don’t miss the next story.
close: And you, dear fathers and mothers: subscribe to our channel, and share these stories with the people you love, so that together we pass on the beautiful message of Islam to our children.
final: Good night, my dears. I entrust you to Allah, with whom nothing entrusted is ever lost.
